last_batch.research: PubMed E-utilities searches covered 30 fresh PCOS self-management topics, with 29 classified as non-prescription candidates. The final query set returned 164 unique PubMed PMIDs, 164 fetched article records, and 164 abstracts available for inspection. Retained numeric intervention-versus-control results or valid relative effects were verified for PMID records: 38988067, 35445067, 39617882, 40869668, 29734548, 41896647, 39143654, 32733258, 33638879, 22808940, 39261845, 37170227, 35059289, 34907435, 30658483, 29946756, 29117618, 27911471, 19585478, 41428718, 33137599, and 35549736. Twenty-two PubMed references were added across 21 new entries. New entries cover high-protein eating, a Mediterranean low-carbohydrate diet, a ketogenic diet, a Mediterranean diet, a low-glycemic diet, time-restricted eating, exercise, aerobic exercise, yoga, mindfulness-based art therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, acupuncture, vitamin D, omega-3, coenzyme Q10, spearmint tea, chasteberry, curcumin, and a mobile health app. The inositol, berberine, and cinnamon topics were linked to existing PCOS evidence entries. Resistance exercise, stress management, sleep intervention, acupressure, massage, probiotics, and patient education were screened out because the selected PubMed records did not provide a retained topic-specific numeric intervention-versus-control magnitude or valid relative effect; N-acetylcysteine was also excluded from this non-prescription batch because its local category is rx. Five truthful thin-study warnings remain for the 47-person aerobic exercise trial, 46-person ketogenic diet trial, 37-person low-glycemic diet trial, 26-person Mediterranean diet trial, and 42-person spearmint trial, including the prior thin-study backlog.
